chunks: He informed me: al-Husayn ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Yahya, from his father, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya, from al-'Amraki, from 'Ali ibn Ja'far, from his brother Musa (peace be upon him).
He said: I asked him about the skink (lizard), the snake, and the gecko that falls into water but does not die — can wudu be performed from it for salat? He said: There is no harm in it.

key_terms.الْعَظَايَةِ: skink/lizard — a small reptile whose falling into water is the subject of this ruling
key_terms.الْوَزَغِ: gecko/wall lizard — a reptile commonly found near water vessels in classical settings
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ بِهِ: there is no harm in it — a standard Imami permissibility formula signalling that the act is ritually valid
key_terms.يُتَوَضَّأُ: passive verb: 'can wudu be performed' — the juristic question posed by 'Ali ibn Ja'far

ai.seo_question: What is the Shia ruling on performing wudu from water in which a lizard, snake, or gecko has fallen but not died?
ai.summary: This hadith, narrated by 'Ali ibn Ja'far from his brother Imam Musa al-Kazim (AS), addresses a jurisprudential question about the ritual purity (taharah) of water into which a reptile has fallen and from which it exits alive. The Imam's ruling — 'lā ba'sa bihi' (there is no harm in it) — establishes that the water remains pure and valid for wudu so long as the animal did not die therein, as death in water is the trigger for najasah.
